# Purpose {.unnumbered}

This notebook evaluates whether the GRIN3D mutation-hotspot prototype produces
stable candidate clusters when two analysis settings are varied:

1. the number of null simulations (`100` through `1,000` in increments of
   `100`); and
2. the minimum AlphaFold pLDDT threshold (`0`, `70`, or `90`).

TP53 serves as the established dense positive-control pattern, while PTEN adds
an independent mutation-rich tumor suppressor. SUZ12, EZH2, and LEF1 represent
sparser mutation patterns across proteins with different lengths and confidence
profiles.

Here, **sparsity** is not a single formal label. It can entail fewer mutation
events or affected subjects, fewer recurrent observations at the same residue,
a low density of altered residues relative to protein length, or mutations that
are widely dispersed in sequence or 3D space. These features have different
statistical consequences: limited event and subject counts reduce power, weak
recurrence makes compact clusters harder to distinguish from random placement,
and spatial dispersion can produce many candidate branches without a compelling
hotspot. Sparsity also makes confidence filtering more consequential because
removing even a modest number of events may represent a large fraction of the
analyzed cohort. Accordingly, the sparse-protein results are interpreted using
retained events and subjects, cluster membership overlap, and p-value convergence
together rather than mutation count alone.

<div class="callout">
**Primary conclusion.** Null-trial count changes Monte Carlo p-values and
significance calls, but not the deterministic observed cluster membership at a
fixed pLDDT threshold. pLDDT filtering can change cluster membership because it
removes coordinates and mutation events, thereby changing the analyzed cohort.
</div>

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  path <- normalizePath(path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(path, "development-code", "GRIN3D_mutation_hotspots.R"))) {
      return(path)
    }
    parent <- dirname(path)
    if (identical(parent, path)) stop("Could not find the repository root")
    path <- parent
  }
}

repo_root <- find_repo_root()
analysis_root <- file.path(repo_root, "analysis", "mutation_plddt_trials")
summary_dir <- file.path(analysis_root, "results", "summary")
figure_dir <- file.path(analysis_root, "results", "figures")

config <- read.csv(file.path(analysis_root, "configurations.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
run_metrics <- read.csv(file.path(summary_dir, "run_metrics.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
convergence <- read.csv(file.path(summary_dir, "trial_convergence_metrics.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pvalue_clusters <- read.csv(file.path(summary_dir, "cluster_pvalue_convergence.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
earliest <- read.csv(file.path(summary_dir, "earliest_significance_convergence.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center", out.width = "100%"
)

display_table <- function(x, digits = 3L, caption = NULL) {
  numeric_columns <- vapply(x, is.numeric, logical(1L))
  x[numeric_columns] <- lapply(x[numeric_columns], function(z) round(z, digits))
  knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE)
}

metric_at <- function(protein, plddt, trials = 1000L) {
  run_metrics[
    run_metrics$protein == protein &
      run_metrics$plddt_threshold == plddt &
      run_metrics$n_sim == trials,
    , drop = FALSE
  ]
}
```

# Results at 1,000 trials

This table is the compact numerical summary of the experiment. `Residues` and
`Events` show retained/total counts. Mean Jaccard compares each condition's
candidate clusters with the unfiltered 1,000-trial cluster landscape for the
same protein.

```{r maximum-trial-results}
maximum_results <- run_metrics[run_metrics$n_sim == 1000, ]
maximum_results <- maximum_results[
  order(match(maximum_results$protein, c("TP53", "PTEN", "SUZ12", "EZH2", "LEF1")),
        maximum_results$plddt_threshold),
]

maximum_display <- data.frame(
  Protein = maximum_results$protein,
  pLDDT = maximum_results$plddt_threshold,
  Residues = paste0(maximum_results$eligible_residues, "/", maximum_results$total_coordinate_residues),
  Events = paste0(maximum_results$mapped_events, "/",
                  maximum_results$mapped_events + maximum_results$excluded_events),
  Subjects = maximum_results$mapped_subjects,
  Clusters = maximum_results$n_clusters,
  Significant = maximum_results$n_significant,
  `Mean Jaccard` = maximum_results$mean_best_jaccard,
  `Median Jaccard` = maximum_results$median_best_jaccard,
  check.names = FALSE
)
display_table(maximum_display, caption = "Results at the maximum evaluated trial count")
```

## Joint p-values at 1,000 trials

The hotspot model reports `p_any_joint`, the final empirical p-value after
accounting for the search across cluster sizes, subject-count thresholds, and
the 1D and 3D cluster trees. The table below summarizes these corrected values;
the minimum identifies the strongest candidate in each condition, while the
median describes the full set of candidate clusters rather than only the
significant tail.

```{r joint-pvalues-1000}
pvalue_1000 <- pvalue_clusters[pvalue_clusters$n_sim == 1000, ]
pvalue_groups <- split(
  pvalue_1000,
  interaction(pvalue_1000$protein, pvalue_1000$plddt_threshold, drop = TRUE)
)

pvalue_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pvalue_groups, function(x) {
  data.frame(
    Protein = x$protein[1],
    pLDDT = x$plddt_threshold[1],
    Clusters = nrow(x),
    `Minimum joint p` = min(x$p_any_joint, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Median joint p` = median(x$p_any_joint, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Clusters p <= 0.05` = sum(x$p_any_joint <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Clusters p <= 0.01` = sum(x$p_any_joint <= 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
pvalue_summary <- pvalue_summary[
  order(match(pvalue_summary$Protein, c("TP53", "PTEN", "SUZ12", "EZH2", "LEF1")),
        pvalue_summary$pLDDT),
]
rownames(pvalue_summary) <- NULL

display_table(
  pvalue_summary,
  digits = 5L,
  caption = "Final joint empirical p-values at 1,000 trials"
)
```

At 1,000 trials, the numbers of corrected significant clusters at pLDDT
0/70/90 are **11/6/6 for TP53**, **0/0/0 for PTEN**, **0/0/2 for SUZ12**,
**0/25/9 for EZH2**, and **9/6/1 for LEF1**. None of the final joint p-values
is at or below 0.01.
Thus, TP53 supplies the clearest unfiltered positive-control signal, PTEN has
no corrected evidence of clustering under these settings, SUZ12 and EZH2
findings are specific to confidence-filtered residue cohorts, and LEF1 retains
corrected clustering evidence in all three cohorts.

With 1,000 total simulations, the analysis uses 500 evaluation simulations,
so the smallest possible uncorrected evaluation p-value is approximately
`r sprintf("%.5f", 1 / 501)`. The observed `p_any_joint` values are larger
because they include the model's search correction; additional trials improve
precision but do not guarantee that a p-value will decrease.

<div class="caution">
Filtering does not merely hide low-confidence residues from a fixed result. It
can exclude mutation events. Comparisons across pLDDT thresholds therefore
represent related but non-identical mutation cohorts.
</div>

# TP53: dense positive-control pattern

## TP53 experiment

The following cell extracts TP53's 1,000-trial results and calculates coordinate
and event retention relative to the unfiltered condition.

```{r tp53-summary}
tp53 <- maximum_results[maximum_results$protein == "TP53", ]
tp53$coordinate_fraction <- tp53$eligible_residues / tp53$total_coordinate_residues
tp53$event_fraction <- tp53$mapped_events / tp53$mapped_events[tp53$plddt_threshold == 0]

display_table(
  tp53[c(
    "plddt_threshold", "eligible_residues", "mapped_events", "mapped_subjects",
    "n_clusters", "n_significant", "coordinate_fraction", "event_fraction",
    "mean_best_jaccard", "reference_recovery_jaccard_0_8"
  )],
  caption = "TP53 structural-confidence sensitivity at 1,000 trials"
)
```

At pLDDT ≥70, TP53 retains `r metric_at('TP53', 70)$mapped_events` of
`r metric_at('TP53', 0)$mapped_events` mutations and has mean cluster Jaccard
`r sprintf('%.3f', metric_at('TP53', 70)$mean_best_jaccard)`. At pLDDT ≥90,
it retains `r metric_at('TP53', 90)$mapped_events` mutations and has mean
Jaccard `r sprintf('%.3f', metric_at('TP53', 90)$mean_best_jaccard)`.

## TP53 p-value and significance convergence

The next figure separates rank stability of empirical p-values from absolute
p-value error.

```{r tp53-convergence-figures, echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "TP53_trial_convergence_overview.png"))
```

**TP53 conclusion:** the exact 1,000-trial significance sets persist from 800
trials without filtering, 700 trials at pLDDT ≥70, and 900 trials at pLDDT ≥90.
The membership itself is invariant within each pLDDT stratum.

At pLDDT ≥70, PTEN retains `r metric_at('PTEN', 70)$mapped_events` of

`r sprintf('%.3f', metric_at('PTEN', 70)$mean_best_jaccard)`. At pLDDT ≥90,

## PTEN p-value and significance convergence

```{r pten-convergence-figure, echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "PTEN_trial_convergence_overview.png"))
```

**PTEN conclusion:** membership is invariant across trial counts at each fixed
threshold. PTEN is also comparatively robust to confidence filtering: mean
Jaccard is `r sprintf('%.3f', metric_at('PTEN', 70)$mean_best_jaccard)` at
pLDDT ≥70 and `r sprintf('%.3f', metric_at('PTEN', 90)$mean_best_jaccard)` at
pLDDT ≥90. No corrected significant clusters occur in any evaluated PTEN
condition. Its exact empty significance sets therefore represent trivial
agreement, not positive evidence of significance convergence.

## LEF1 trial convergence

```{r lef1-convergence-figures, echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "LEF1_trial_convergence_overview.png"))
```

**LEF1 conclusion:** candidate membership is invariant across trial counts at

at ≥70 and `r sprintf('%.3f', metric_at('LEF1', 90)$mean_best_jaccard)` at ≥90)
because only 27 and 26 of the original 50 events remain. The convergence result
is therefore encouraging within each threshold, but filtered and unfiltered
LEF1 results should be interpreted as different mutation cohorts.

# Cross-protein interpretation

## Interactive cluster stability explorer

Use the controls below to compare the strongest candidate clusters for each
protein and pLDDT threshold. The matrix tracks corrected joint p-values across
trial counts. Its rows do not change within a pLDDT threshold because observed
cluster construction is deterministic; changes in color show Monte Carlo
p-value convergence. Clicking a cell links that candidate to its best
residue-overlap match at pLDDT 0, 70, and 90, revealing how structural filtering
changes cluster membership. The residue-track comparison uses the 1,000-trial
candidate sets, and the matrix can display up to the 40 strongest candidates
ranked at 1,000 trials.

```{r interactive-cluster-explorer, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
source(file.path(analysis_root, "interactive_cluster_explorer.R"))
explorer_html <- build_cluster_explorer(
  pvalue_clusters = pvalue_clusters,
  run_metrics = run_metrics,
  template_file = file.path(analysis_root, "interactive_cluster_explorer.html")
)
cat("```{=html}\n", explorer_html, "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

## Cluster membership sensitivity

This figure puts all proteins on the same scale. Within each threshold, the
line is flat across trial counts because cluster construction precedes null
calibration. Differences between pLDDT lines quantify structural-filtering
sensitivity.

```{r global-sensitivity, echo=FALSE, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(
  figure_dir,
  paste0(c("TP53", "PTEN", "SUZ12", "EZH2", "LEF1"), "_global_sensitivity.png")
))
```

## P-value rank and significance-set convergence

Spearman correlation measures whether clusters retain the same p-value ranking
as the 1,000-trial result at the same pLDDT. Exact significance-set matching is
stricter: every corrected significant cluster must agree.

```{r earliest-significance-table}
earliest_display <- earliest
names(earliest_display) <- c(
  "Protein", "pLDDT", "Earliest persistent exact match",
  "Significant clusters at 1,000", "Interpretation"
)
display_table(earliest_display)
```

A match first reached at exactly 1,000 trials cannot demonstrate persistence,
because no later evaluated trial count exists. Conditions with zero significant
clusters have trivial agreement on an empty set rather than positive evidence
of statistical convergence.

## Do p-values decrease as trials increase?

Not necessarily. For `B` evaluation simulations and `b` null outcomes at least
as extreme as the observed cluster, the empirical estimate is approximately
`p = (1 + b) / (1 + B)`. Adding simulations increases both the possible
denominator and the opportunity to observe additional extreme null outcomes.
An individual p-value can therefore decrease, increase, or remain unchanged.

What reliably improves is **resolution**. GRIN3D reserves half of each run for
evaluation, so the smallest attainable evaluation p-value becomes progressively
smaller as the total trial count rises.

```{r empirical-pvalue-resolution}
resolution <- unique(run_metrics[c(
  "n_sim", "n_evaluation", "minimum_empirical_p"
)])
resolution <- resolution[order(resolution$n_sim), ]
names(resolution) <- c("Total trials", "Evaluation trials", "Minimum empirical p")
display_table(resolution, digits = 5L,
              caption = "Monte Carlo resolution available at each trial count")
```

```{r empirical-pvalue-resolution-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
plot(
  resolution$`Total trials`, resolution$`Minimum empirical p`,
  type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2, col = "#2166AC", log = "y",
  xlab = "Total null-simulation trials",
  ylab = "Minimum attainable empirical p-value",
  main = "Increasing trials improves small-p-value resolution"
)
grid()
```

The next cell directly compares every candidate cluster's 100-trial p-value
with its p-value in the 1,000-trial reference at the same protein and pLDDT.
This demonstrates that decreasing p-values are common—especially for the
strongest clusters—but are not a mathematical requirement.

```{r pvalue-direction-100-vs-1000}
initial_pvalues <- pvalue_clusters[pvalue_clusters$n_sim == 100, ]
delta <- initial_pvalues$reference_p_any_joint - initial_pvalues$p_any_joint
initial_pvalues$direction <- ifelse(
  delta < -1e-12, "Lower at 1,000",
  ifelse(delta > 1e-12, "Higher at 1,000", "Unchanged")
)

direction_groups <- split(
  initial_pvalues,
  interaction(initial_pvalues$protein, initial_pvalues$plddt_threshold, drop = TRUE)
)
direction_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(direction_groups, function(z) {
  counts <- table(factor(
    z$direction,
    levels = c("Lower at 1,000", "Higher at 1,000", "Unchanged")
  ))
  data.frame(
    Protein = z$protein[[1L]], pLDDT = z$plddt_threshold[[1L]],
    `Lower at 1,000` = unname(counts[[1L]]),
    `Higher at 1,000` = unname(counts[[2L]]),
    Unchanged = unname(counts[[3L]]),
    `Total clusters` = nrow(z), check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
direction_summary <- direction_summary[
  order(match(direction_summary$Protein, c("TP53", "PTEN", "SUZ12", "EZH2", "LEF1")),
        direction_summary$pLDDT),
]
display_table(direction_summary,
              caption = "Direction of p-value change from 100 to 1,000 trials")
```

```{r pvalue-direction-overall}
overall_direction <- table(factor(
  initial_pvalues$direction,
  levels = c("Lower at 1,000", "Higher at 1,000", "Unchanged")
))
significant_reference <- initial_pvalues[initial_pvalues$reference_significant_any, ]
significant_direction <- table(factor(
  significant_reference$direction,
  levels = c("Lower at 1,000", "Higher at 1,000", "Unchanged")
))

pvalue_direction_conclusion <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("All candidate clusters", "Significant in the 1,000-trial reference"),
  `Lower at 1,000` = c(overall_direction[[1L]], significant_direction[[1L]]),
  `Higher at 1,000` = c(overall_direction[[2L]], significant_direction[[2L]]),
  Unchanged = c(overall_direction[[3L]], significant_direction[[3L]]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
display_table(pvalue_direction_conclusion)
```

Across all conditions, `r overall_direction[[1L]]` cluster estimates were lower
at 1,000 trials, `r overall_direction[[2L]]` were higher, and
`r overall_direction[[3L]]` were unchanged. All
`r nrow(significant_reference)` cluster instances significant in their
1,000-trial reference had lower p-values than at 100 trials. Thus the strongest
signals benefited from added resolution, while the full collection demonstrates
that monotonic reduction is not a general rule.

<div class="callout">
**Interpretation.** Increasing trials refines the null estimate and permits
smaller measurable p-values. It does not create new observed clusters, and it
does not guarantee that every p-value moves downward. The relevant objective is
convergence of p-values and significance decisions, not monotonic reduction.
</div>

# Recommendations

1. Treat observed cluster membership as reproducible candidate generation when
   the structural input and pLDDT threshold are fixed.
2. Report empirical p-values separately from cluster membership. Trial count
   changes Monte Carlo resolution even when cluster residues are unchanged.
3. Use pLDDT ≥70 as a sensitivity analysis and report retained residues,
   mutations, and subjects alongside every filtered result.
4. Use pLDDT ≥90 as a stringent stress test, not an automatically preferred
   primary analysis.
5. Do not treat a significance set that appears for the first time at 1,000
   trials as converged. Extend those conditions beyond 1,000 trials.
6. Repeat final analyses with independent random seeds to measure Monte Carlo
   variability; the present nested fixed-seed runs measure resolution behavior.
7. Keep biological annotation as a separate evidence layer from statistical
   significance.

<div class="callout">
**Handoff summary.** The prototype is ready for documented exploratory hotspot
discovery and sensitivity evaluation. The evidence does not yet support treating
every corrected significance call as final, especially where convergence is
first observed only at the 1,000-trial endpoint or confidence filtering removes
a large portion of the event cohort.
</div>

The simulation results are already saved. To regenerate only this notebook:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
conda run -n kids26-team13 Rscript -e \
```

Primary files used by the notebook:

- `configurations.csv`: declared experiment grid and input paths;
- `results/summary/run_metrics.csv`: one row per configuration;
- `results/summary/trial_convergence_metrics.csv`: p-value convergence metrics;
- `results/summary/cluster_pvalue_convergence.csv`: cluster-level p-value trajectories;
- `results/summary/earliest_significance_convergence.csv`: exact-set stability;
- `results/figures/`: precomputed overlap and convergence figures.
